newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso weak but respects 8.00/dlr mark.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso weak but respects 8.00/dlr mark.

text.p: The Mexican peso was still weaker across the board at mid-morning trade on Friday in what traders said was a speculative, volatile market. Nonetheless, they said, the peso had shied away from trading at eight to the dollar.
"Its like crazy, the market is very skittish," a trader said. "The peso has hit the eight-per dollar market, twice, but has respected it."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart stood 1.6 and 2.0 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9800/7.9840 and 7.9750/7.9800 per dollar.
Several dealers said they saw a big player step in to sell dollars each time the peso flirted with the psychological eight-per-dollar barrier.
The 48-hour contract had earlier weakened to 7.9920/7.9950 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed 3.95 centavos weaker at 7.9670/7.9720 per dollar.
"If you're a big bank with hefty (dollar) positions), then you can move the market," another dealer said.
Dealers also said the peso halted its slide when the U.S. long bond recovered from being down 7/32 to climbing 21/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
